effects.label: Restore
effects.fixes: Mixed damage at once: compression, soft focus, noise, tape and sepia casts, flicker, dirt and scratches.
effects.not: It invents fine detail where the damage destroyed it. Describe the period, place, light and materials: the prompt steers what it fills in.

proof.label: Restore
proof.alt: Three panels: a 1970s family picnic made to look like old faded, scratched home-movie film; the LTX restore; the clean original render.
proof.looked: Scratches, dust, flicker, grain and the sepia fade are all gone, and three laughing men on a red checked blanket come back in full colour and focus, in the original's places. Better on all three measures: VMAF 0 to 39.
proof.fault: It invents what the fade destroyed: the khaki shirts come back as patterned short-sleeve shirts and the grass much greener than the original.
proof.damage: an old home-movie look added with ffmpeg to a fresh render: faded sepia colour, flicker, soft focus, grain, two moving scratches and CRF 34 compression
proof.clip: a fresh LTX-2.5 text-to-video render made for this proof
proof.prompt: a family picnic on a sunny lawn in the 1970s, three adults in summer clothes laughing on a red checked blanket, a wicker basket, leafy trees, warm afternoon light

more.alt: Three panels: the greenhouse clip damaged with blur, grain and heavy compression; the LTX restore; the clean original.
more.looked: Blocks, grain and blur are gone and the glass grid is crisp again through the whole push-in. It re-draws rather than recovers: the fog turns cyan and the sky darker, with more contrast than the original. That is why PSNR and SSIM fall while VMAF climbs from 0 to 59.
more.fault: Colour and fog drift away from the original, and small roof panes are invented, not recovered.
more.damage: Gaussian blur (sigma 2.5), film-grain noise (14) and H.264 CRF 40

effects.label: Deblur
effects.fixes: Out-of-focus footage: lens defocus, Gaussian and box blur.
effects.not: Motion blur, heavy compression and noise are out of its scope. Extreme blur gets made up, not recovered.

proof.label: Deblur
proof.alt: Three panels: a cyclist in a red jacket on a seaside promenade, thrown out of focus; the LTX deblur; the clean original render.
proof.looked: The rider's face, helmet, the bike's spokes and frame, the railings and the palm trunks come back sharp, matching the original. Better on all three measures: PSNR up 2.1 dB, SSIM 0.89 to 0.94, VMAF 8 to 66.
proof.fault: The far background stays a little softer than the original.
proof.damage: lens-style defocus (Gaussian blur, sigma 4) added to a fresh render. The Deblur card covers defocus, not motion blur, so this is defocus

effects.label: Remove compression
effects.fixes: Macroblocking, chroma bleed, ringing and banding from low-bitrate video.
effects.not: Not blur, noise, upscaling or colour. Far above 960x544 the effect weakens.

proof.label: Remove compression
proof.alt: Three panels: the greenhouse clip crushed by heavy H.264 compression; the LTX repair; the clean original.
proof.looked: Macroblocks and smeared edges are gone. The glass grid comes out crisper than the soft original, which costs 1.7 dB of PSNR while SSIM and VMAF rise.
proof.fault: It adds sharpening and pane texture the original never had.

more.looked: The blocks are gone and it looks clean, but the repaired foliage is re-drawn. Here it is no closer to the original on any of the three measures (VMAF 28 to 27).
more.fault: On dense foliage the repair invents leaf detail instead of recovering it.

effects.label: Colorize
effects.not: The colours are the model's guess, steered by your words; they are not the real colours of the day. Lower the strength to 0.8-0.9 if colour bleeds.

proof.label: Colorize
proof.alt: Three panels: a 1950s tram street in black and white; the LTX colorized clip; the original colour render.
proof.looked: Red and green striped awnings, the green and cream tram, blue coats and warm brick come back from pure grey, following the words, with every walker and the tram kept in place. It comes out more vivid than our rather muted original, so its colour distance to the original rises (CIEDE2000 5.1 to 8.2) even as the chroma goes from 0 to 8.7.
proof.fault: Brighter and greener than the original: the colours are the model's reading of the words, not a recovery.
proof.damage: every colour taken out (ffmpeg hue=s=0) from a fresh colour render

effects.label: Upscale x2
effects.fixes: Twice the width and height of a clean low-resolution clip.
effects.not: It makes up new detail rather than recovering the real thing, so the card says not to use it where faithfulness to live-action footage matters.

proof.label: Upscale x2

crops.alt: The same crop of the tapestry from a Lanczos x2, the LTX x2 and the original, enlarged pixel for pixel.

effects.label: SDR to HDR
effects.fixes: Ordinary SDR video to scene-linear HDR: an HLG BT.2020 10-bit master, half-float ACEScg EXR frames and a ProRes 4444 HLG master.
effects.not: No prompt: a fixed scene embedding drives it. It works on the whole frame, and a long or large clip can run out of memory in the decoder.

proof.label: SDR to HDR
proof.alt: Three panels: a fishing harbour at sunset, SDR source; the HDR result tone-mapped back to SDR; a map of where the HDR result is brighter than SDR white, yellow to red.
proof.looked: The sun, the glowing sky around it and the glitter path on the water are lifted well above SDR white while the boats and the water stay where they were. Tone-mapped back to SDR it matches the source. All three masters were checked: HLG BT.2020 10-bit, ProRes 4444 HLG and 97 half-float ACEScg EXR frames.
proof.fault: The headroom is all in the sun and the sky; on an SDR screen the result looks like the source.
proof.damage: none: a fresh SDR BT.709 render

note: Every number was measured by scripts/prove_finish.py on this machine, on AI-generated showcase clips damaged on purpose with ffmpeg. PSNR, SSIM and VMAF compare each frame with the clean original: PSNR punishes any re-drawn detail, VMAF is Netflix's perceptual score. The look notes are ours, from watching every result.
